newsitem.title: INDIA: Film-maker Nihalani welcomes Magsaysay for Devi.
newsitem.headline: Film-maker Nihalani welcomes Magsaysay for Devi.

text.p: Film-maker Govind Nihalani on Thursday welcomed news that Bengali writer Mahashweta Devi, whose landmark novel he is filming, had won the Magsaysay Award.

"I think it's an eminently deserved award," the renowned film-maker told Reuters. "For her, the next step should be a Nobel Prize. It's indeed long-overdue recognition in the case of Mahashweta Devi."
"It is committed literature, and that is one of its strengths," he added. "But also in terms of style, literary value, it is very modern, very dynamic."

Nihalani, who interrupted his shooting of Devi's book -- "Hazar Chaurashir Maa" ("Mother of 1084") -- added: "This award, with the kind of impact it has had in our country, will bring her literature to the attention of the whole world."

Jaya Bachchan, widely considered one of India's most sensitive actresses, is playing the role of the eponymous mother. Newcomers Joy Sengupta and Nandita Das make their first appearances as the ill-fated activist son and his girlfriend.
Nihalani said he was in the middle of shooting the sequence where the mother meets her son's girlfriend for the first time, and they have just exchanged the first few words.

Asked if he believed that Mahashweta Devi's work had really aroused concern for the problems of Indian tribals, Nihalani said: "Any person who reads her work comes to understand the concerns of tribal people, the tribal environment. You cannot remain unaffected by it.
"It forces a person to think, to take a fresh look at their problems," he added. "It breaks through the stereotyped picture of the tribals."
Nihalani said he expected the film to be ready for commercial release by the end of the year.
"It's being filmed on a shoestring budget, with no support from the usual film financiers," he said, adding that the cost had not yet been worked out.
